explanation: ACQUIESCE is correctly spelled with a C after ACQUI and ends in -ESCE. It means to accept something reluctantly but without protest.
CONSCIENTIOUS has the letter sequence C-O-N-S-C-I-E-N-T-I-O-U-S. It contains the word conscience and the suffix -ious, meaning wishing to do what is right.
DESICCATE has a single S and double C. It means to remove all moisture from something. A common error is writing dessicate (double S) by analogy with dessert.
EMBARRASSMENT has double R and double S. A useful memory aid: it is Really Really embarrassing to get this wrong (double R, double S).
FAHRENHEIT is a proper noun (German physicist Gabriel Fahrenheit) with the unusual letter sequence -HEIT. It is frequently misspelled with only one H or wrong vowel order.
GARRULOUS has double R in the middle and ends in -OUS. It means excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.
HAEMORRHAGE (British) uses AE at the start, double R in the middle, and -RHAGE at the end. The American spelling is hemorrhage. It means a heavy discharge of blood.
IDIOSYNCRASY ends in -RASY not -RACY. It refers to a mode of behaviour or way of thought peculiar to an individual. The -CRASY ending confuses writers who think of democracy.
IRRELEVANT has double R (from the prefix IR- + RELEVANT) and ends in -ANT not -ENT. It means not connected with or relevant to something.
JEOPARDISE (British) or JEOPARDIZE (American) has the unusual letter sequence J-E-O-P. It means to put someone or something into a situation in which there is a danger of harm or loss.
KNOWLEDGEABLE retains the E before -ABLE to preserve the soft G sound. Dropping the E would make it look like it should be pronounced with a hard G.
LIQUEFY ends in -EFY not -IFY. It is one of a small group of exceptions where the suffix is -EFY: liquefy, stupefy, rarefy, and putrefy.
MILLENNIUM has double L and double N. The word comes from Latin mille (thousand) + annus (year), with the -ENNIUM suffix meaning period of years.
NAUSEOUS ends in -SEOUS, following the pattern of NAUSEA + -OUS. It means causing or affected by nausea.
OCCURRENCE has double C and double R, plus the -ENCE ending. The base verb OCCUR doubles the R when adding -ENCE or -ENCE suffixes.
PERSEVERANCE ends in -ANCE not -ENCE. The word contains PERSEVERE + -ANCE. It means continuing despite difficulty; steadfastness.
QUESTIONNAIRE (from French) has double N and double R and ends in -AIRE. It is frequently misspelled by dropping one N or one R.
RENAISSANCE comes from French renaitre (to be reborn) and has double S in the middle. It refers to the cultural and intellectual revival of classical learning in 14th-17th century Europe.
SUPERSEDE ends in -SEDE not -CEDE. It is the only common English word ending in -SEDE; most others end in -CEDE (precede, concede) or -CEED (proceed, succeed).
TEMPERAMENT has 4 syllables: TEM-per-a-ment. A common error is to omit the A, writing temperment. The A in the third syllable is often elided in speech but must be retained in writing.
UNNECESSARY has double N (from UN- + NECESSARY) and double S in NECESSARY. Remember: one Collar, two Socks - one C and two Ss in necessary.
VACCINATION has double C and a single N. The word comes from VACCINE + -ATION. Vaccine itself comes from Latin vacca (cow), after Jenner used cowpox to vaccinate against smallpox.
WITHHOLD has double H because it is formed from WITH + HOLD. When two words are joined and the first ends with the same letter the second starts with, both letters are retained.
XENOPHOBIA starts with X (from Greek xenos, meaning stranger) and ends with -PHOBIA (from Greek phobos, meaning fear). It means dislike of or prejudice against people from other countries.
YACHT has a silent CH, pronounced /jɒt/. It comes from Dutch jacht, short for jachtschip (hunting ship). The CH is retained in spelling but not in pronunciation.
ZEALOUS is spelled with EA and ends in -OUS. It means having or showing great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective.

questionText: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning unable to be believed?
explanation: INCREDIBLE ends in -IBLE not -ABLE. A useful rule: if the base word ends in -ION (not directly applicable here), use -IBLE. Incredible comes from Latin incredibilis.

questionText: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning occurring once every two years?
explanation: BIENNIAL has double N and ends in -IAL. It means occurring once every two years. Compare with biannual (occurring twice a year) - these two words are often confused.
BUREAUCRACY contains the French-origin BUREAU (with the unusual E-A-U vowel sequence) plus -CRACY. The AU sound in bureau is pronounced /oʊ/, contributing to frequent misspelling.
CONNOISSEUR (from French) has double N, double S, and the -EUR ending. It refers to an expert judge in matters of taste, especially in fine arts or food and wine.
DILEMMA has double M and ends in -A, not -NA (a common error). It comes from Greek dilemma (double proposition) and means a situation in which a difficult choice must be made.
EXHILARATING has a silent H after EX, a single L, and ends in -ATING. It comes from Latin exhilarare (to gladden) and means making one feel very happy and animated.
FLUORESCENT has the vowel sequence U-O after FL, and ends in -ESCENT. It describes something that emits bright light; a common confusion is with FLOURESCENT (incorrect).
EXAGGERATE has double G in the middle. It comes from Latin exaggerare (to heap up) and means to represent as greater than it really is. A single G is the most common error.

questionText: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning a forecast of the future?
explanation: PROGNOSIS has a single G and single N and S, ending in -OSIS. It comes from Greek prognosis (foreknowledge) and refers to a medical forecast of the likely outcome of a disease.
CONSCIENTIOUS contains the word SCIENCE within it (con-SCIENCE-tious) and ends in -OUS. It means wishing to do what is right, especially to do ones work well.
PARAPHERNALIA has PH (not F) in the middle and ends in -IA. Originally a legal term for a wife property beyond her dowry, it now means miscellaneous articles.
MISCELLANEOUS has double L and ends in -EOUS (not -IOUS). It means composed of members or elements of different kinds; of mixed composition.
ACCOMMODATE has double C and double M. It is one of the most commonly misspelled words in English. A useful memory aid: it can Accommodate double letters in both CC and MM.
CARIBBEAN has a single R and double B, ending in -EAN. It is frequently misspelled with double R. The word derives from the Carib people, the indigenous inhabitants of the region.
MEDITERRANEAN has single D, double T in the middle, double R, and ends in -EAN. It comes from Latin mediterraneus meaning in the middle of the earth.
PARTICULARLY ends in -ARLY not -ARILY. It is the adverb form of PARTICULAR + -LY. A common error is to insert an extra I, writing particularily.
RECONNAISSANCE (French origin) has double N, double S, and ends in -ANCE. It means military observation of an area to locate an enemy or ascertain strategic features.
SEPARATE is spelled with an A in the middle: sep-A-rate. A very common error is writing sepErate. A useful memory aid: there is A PAR in separAte.
SILHOUETTE (French origin) has LH after SI, then the -OUETTE ending. It refers to a dark shape against a lighter background, named after French finance minister Etienne de Silhouette.
SOUVENIR (from French) has the vowel sequence OU and ends in -EIR. It means a thing that is kept as a reminder of a person, place, or event.
TYRANNY has a single R and double N. It comes from Greek tyrannos (absolute ruler) and means cruel and oppressive government or rule.
MISCELLANEOUS has double L (not double N) and ends in -EOUS. The double L comes from the Latin root miscellus (mixed) via miscellaneus.

questionText: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning the study of ancient writings?
explanation: PALAEOGRAPHY (British spelling) uses AE for the classical Greek diphthong and ends in -GRAPHY (from Greek graphein, to write). It is the study of ancient writing systems.
MISCHIEVOUS ends in -VOUS not -VIOUS. It comes from MISCHIEF + -OUS. A very common error is to insert an I before OUS, writing mischievIOUS - this is always wrong.
